On November 18, Hollywood Park and the Rams handed turkeys and grocery boxes to the first 2,500 cars in the Red Zone at SoFi, with captain Quentin Lake on hand. Teresa Ocampo was out there waving cars through, and she's carried that same energy into a Wednesday night home date with the Packers.

The Formula: Net ratings Los Angeles Rams 2.3, Green Bay Packers −3.7 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 24, 2026).

The Rams have won four straight, at Las Vegas, against the Chargers, at Washington and 34-6 at Arizona, and they've allowed 187 points in ten games, well short of Green Bay's 221. Matthew Stafford has 19 touchdown throws and Kyren Williams has 616 rushing yards with six touchdowns behind him. The Rams will do it without Puka Nacua, who is on injured reserve after knee surgery, according to the latest injury listings.

Gus Lindqvist has a real answer from Green Bay. Jordan Love has 20 touchdown throws against seven interceptions, and Christian Watson has 916 yards and seven scores. Teresa gets her home win on the night before Thanksgiving. Gus gets ten days of Watson film, and he heads back to De Pere still telling people the ice melted for him.

games.fanatic_story:
Teresa Ocampo already did her Thanksgiving good deed in the Red Zone at SoFi Stadium. On November 18 she waved cars through the Hollywood Park and Rams turkey drive, the one that fed the first 2,500 cars, and she still swears Quentin Lake handed a frozen bird through a minivan window like it was a fourth-down snap.

Gus Lindqvist flew in from De Pere with a carry-on full of cheese curds and a grievance about the weather. Back home, Titletown had to rebuild the skating ice on Hy-Vee Plaza last weekend because it got too warm. Too warm. In Green Bay. In late November.

Gus: The ice outside Lambeau melted, and I still flew somewhere it's going to be seventy-two degrees at kickoff. My brother-in-law has already made a meme about it.

Teresa: Wear the sunglasses you pretend you don't own. Nobody here will tell.

So here's the night before Thanksgiving in Inglewood. Two teams with matching records, six wins and four losses apiece, and both coming off last Sunday on the couch. Ten days to stew is a long time for a football fan, and the two of them stewed in opposite directions.

Gus spent his ten days on Minnesota. The last thing his Packers did was get shoved around at Lambeau by the Vikings, a loss so ugly he took the long way home so the neighbors wouldn't see his face. Teresa spent hers in a parade of highlights. The Rams have won four straight: in Las Vegas, against the Chargers, in Washington, and then a beatdown in Arizona she replays on her phone at red lights.

Teresa: Four in a row. Kyren Williams runs like he's late for dinner.

Gus: Christian Watson has nine hundred and sixteen receiving yards. Look it up. Seven touchdowns. He runs past people the way my uncle runs past a salad.

That one stings, because it's true. Watson has been the reason Jordan Love can throw it deep without blinking. Love has twenty touchdown throws and only seven interceptions, and Gus treats that interception count the way some people treat a family heirloom. He won't let anyone touch it.

Teresa's counter is Matthew Stafford, who has nineteen touchdown throws, and the Rams defense, which has given up fewer points than the Packers have. She also has Byron Young, who keeps showing up in the backfield like he got a calendar invite.

Gus: Lukas Van Ness has six sacks. Evan Williams has eighty-four tackles. We tackle in Green Bay. It's a cultural thing.

Teresa: You also got run off your own field by Minnesota.

Gus: We don't talk about the Vikings at the dinner table, Teresa. That's a family rule.

Here's what neither of them says out loud. The Rams have been better on the road than at SoFi this season, and that bugs Teresa more than she admits. The building is gorgeous, the screen is enormous, and the home crowd has watched more losses than wins. Gus knows the Packers have taken care of business away from Lambeau, winning three of five, including a big day in New England.

So the night comes down to a simple question. Can Love and Watson get loose against a defense that hasn't let anybody get loose for a month? Or does Stafford get the early lead, hand it to Williams, and let the crowd do the rest while everybody's thinking about pie?

Teresa's plan is to be home by ten, brine the turkey at midnight, and wake up thankful. Gus's plan is to sleep on her couch and insist the cheese curds count as a side dish.

Gus: If we win, I'm telling everybody back home it was colder here than Green Bay.

Teresa: It's seventy-two degrees.

Gus: In my heart, it's a frozen tundra.

My call: Rams 26, Packers 20.

games.fanatic_story:
Darnell Whitfield has staked out the same curb on Woodward Avenue since he was nine, and this Thursday the curb is part of history. America's Thanksgiving Parade steps off at 8:45 in the morning for the 100th time, with Dan Gilbert as grand marshal, 33 floats, five giant balloons and a brand-new Big Head of Jeff Daniels bobbing down the street like it owns the place.

Kasia Nowicki drove in from Berwyn on Wednesday night with a thermos of coffee, a folding chair and a Bears stocking cap she refuses to take off indoors.

Kasia: A hundred parades. Do you know how many times you've told me about the World War Two years?

Darnell: Twice a year. They skipped it in 1943 and 1944, which is why number one hundred lands now and not two years ago. History matters, Kasia.

Kasia: So does the fourth quarter.

Darnell will walk from the end of the parade route at Congress Street straight to Ford Field, the way his dad did, and Kasia will follow him because she has nowhere else to stand. That's the Detroit Thanksgiving: balloons in the morning, football by one, and somebody's aunt texting about the gravy the whole time.

This one is the real thing, too. These two have the same record, eight wins and two losses, and the winner sits alone on top of the division going into December. Both teams played Sunday. Nobody is fresh, and nobody cares.

Darnell's case starts at home. The Lions haven't lost at Ford Field all season. Six games, six wins, if you count the trip to Munich that went down as a home date, and Darnell absolutely counts it. Jahmyr Gibbs has 1,098 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, and Darnell describes every one of them by pointing at the sky and saying "gone."

Darnell: Gibbs touches the ball in space and the whole building stands up at once. You can feel it in the concrete.

Kasia: Caleb Williams can make the whole building sit back down.

She means it. Williams has been sharp when it counts. The Bears have won five in a row, and the run started with a road win in Atlanta and hasn't stopped. D'Andre Swift has 10 rushing touchdowns, Luther Burden III has turned into the guy Williams looks for on third down, and Jeffery Simmons leads the defense in sacks.

Darnell counters with Amon-Ra St. Brown, who has eight touchdown catches and the best hands in the state, and Jared Goff, who has thrown 20 touchdowns with only four interceptions. Darnell has the interception count tattooed on his memory. He brings it up the way other people bring up the weather.

Kasia: You know what I remember? Week Two. We lost to Minnesota and I didn't speak to anyone for a day. Then we figured it out. We're tougher now.

Darnell: You were tougher in Seattle. Thursday you're at Ford Field with a hundred parades worth of noise in the building.

Kasia doesn't love that part. Both teams have scored plenty this fall, and both defenses have had a few long Sundays. She's convinced this turns into a slugfest instead of a shootout, because division games on short weeks always end up with somebody bleeding on the turf in the fourth quarter. Darnell thinks Gibbs gets loose once, maybe twice, and that's all it takes.

The plan is simple. Parade at 8:45, stuffing at the half, family arguments after. Darnell brought an extra Honolulu blue scarf for Kasia in case she wants to switch sides by the second quarter.

Kasia: I'd rather walk home to Berwyn.

Darnell: That's a long walk. You'll miss pie.

Kasia: I'll take my chances.

When the last balloon drifts past Congress and the stadium fills up, Darnell expects Detroit to do what it has done at home all season. Kasia expects to sweat out every snap until the clock hits zero, and in a game this close, she probably will.

My call: Lions 27, Bears 24.

games.fanatic_story:
Rhonda Castillo has watched every Cowboys Thanksgiving halftime show since Reba McEntire opened the whole tradition at Texas Stadium in 1997, and she has opinions about all thirty of them. This year's headliner for the Salvation Army Red Kettle Kickoff is Miranda Lambert, raised in East Texas about an hour from Dallas, and Rhonda has decided that a hometown girl on the halftime stage is a sign.

Vinnie Scarpa flew down from South Philadelphia on Tuesday night, mostly to argue with her in person. He brought a soft pretzel in his jacket pocket for luck. It's been in there since the airport.

Vinnie: You think a country singer decides a football game?

Rhonda: I think a Texas girl at halftime in Arlington on Thanksgiving doesn't happen by accident. Also, we beat you by seventeen in your own building last month.

That's the part Vinnie doesn't love. The Cowboys went into Philadelphia in October and ran the Eagles off their own field, and the Eagles then lost two more before they finally found a win. Seven losses in a row, start to finish. Vinnie stopped answering texts from his cousins around Halloween.

Then last Sunday happened. The Eagles beat Pittsburgh by three, Joe Milton III had the ball in his hands, and Vinnie walked out of the Linc like a man who'd been let out of jail.

Vinnie: One win. That's all I needed. Milton's got the strongest arm I've seen in green in years. He throws a deep ball that comes down with snow on it.

Rhonda: He'll be throwing it to Caleb Downs.

She's not wrong to feel good. Dak Prescott has 25 touchdown throws and only six interceptions. CeeDee Lamb has 1,108 receiving yards and nine scores, and Javonte Williams has run for 10 touchdowns. This Dallas team can score from anywhere, and it showed it Sunday by dropping fifty-one on Tennessee.

Vinnie: You also gave up forty-six to San Francisco the week before. Your defense has a revolving door.

Rhonda: Quinnen Williams has eight sacks. Tell Milton to bring a helmet with extra padding.

That's the honest truth about these Cowboys. They are thrilling and maddening in the same afternoon, a team that has scored a ton and given up nearly as much. Rhonda has a rule about Thanksgiving games: never leave the couch until the clock is all zeros, because this team has made her cry in the fourth quarter more than once this year.

Vinnie, for his part, knows the Eagles don't have the firepower to trade touchdowns all day. What they have is Nolan Smith Jr., who has six sacks, and a defense that wants to make this ugly, even with Zack Baun on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley have had quieter years than anybody in Philadelphia expected, and Vinnie would like a word with the football gods about that.

Vinnie: Just keep it close into the fourth. Make Dak earn it. That's our whole plan.

Rhonda: Your whole plan is hoping.

Vinnie: Hoping got us one win. I'll ride it.

Here's what both of them agree on. The red kettles come out at halftime, Miranda Lambert sings, and everybody watching gets asked to give something to people who need it this winter. Rhonda has already put a twenty in the kettle outside her grocery store in Grand Prairie. Vinnie says he'll match it if the Eagles keep it within one score.

Rhonda: That's not how charity works, Vincent.

Vinnie: It's how Philadelphia works.

The turkey will be dry, the arguments will be loud, and the Cowboys will probably need a late stop to put the Eagles away. Rhonda will be on her feet for it. Vinnie will be holding a cold pretzel and praying.

My call: Cowboys 27, Eagles 22.

games.fanatic_story:
Marty Kowalczyk will run eight kilometers through downtown Buffalo on Thursday morning and then sit in a cold seat in Orchard Park for three more hours that night, and he calls that a balanced holiday. The YMCA Turkey Trot turns 131 this year. It's the oldest consecutively run footrace in the world, and for the first time in a generation it has a new course, a single loop that starts and ends at the Buffalo Convention Center and still sends the runners down Delaware Avenue for the back half.

Della Ruiz came in from Overland Park on Tuesday and was informed, at the baggage claim, that she would be running too.

Della: I flew here for football. Nobody said anything about cardio.

Marty: Fourteen thousand people do it every year. Little kids. Grandmothers in turkey hats. You'll be fine. Just don't wear the red jacket, people will think you're lost.

Della: I'm wearing the red jacket to the game, Marty. I'm wearing it to the race. I might wear it to dinner.

This is the game both of them circled in August. The Bills have nine wins and one loss. The Chiefs have eight and two. It's Thanksgiving night, the whole country is full of turkey and watching, and somebody is going to walk out of Highmark Stadium holding the inside track to January.

Marty's whole argument is Josh Allen and the run game nobody in Kansas City wants to talk about. James Cook III has 1,060 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, and Marty has started calling him "the Fourth of July" because every carry looks like a fireworks show. Greg Rousseau has 10 sacks. The Bills have won six straight since a home loss to New England, and Marty still won't say the word "Patriots" indoors.

Della: Patrick Mahomes has twenty-two touchdown throws and four interceptions. Four. You know how many your guy has thrown?

Marty: We don't count those in Western New York. It's bad luck.

Della's not just talking about Mahomes, though. The Kansas City defense has given up fewer points than Buffalo's has, and Nick Bolton is everywhere. George Karlaftis has eight sacks. Kenneth Walker III has given the Chiefs a ground game Della keeps describing as "rude."

Della: We play defense now. Mahomes doesn't have to win it by himself. He just has to win it at the end.

Marty: He's done that to us enough times. You don't have to remind me.

That's the history neither of them wants to say out loud. Marty has been to too many January nights where Mahomes had the ball last. He knows the feeling in his stomach when the clock gets inside two minutes and the red jerseys start celebrating. He's trying very hard to convince himself this year is different, and the record says it might be.

The forecast says the sky might open up Thursday night, and Marty is quietly thrilled. Rain in late November in Orchard Park means a slippery ball, a lot of handoffs and a crowd that refuses to sit down. Della packed a poncho. Marty told her ponchos are for tourists.

Della: I am a tourist.

Marty: Not tonight. Tonight you're a Bills fan who's wearing the wrong jacket.

They'll eat turkey sandwiches in the parking lot at five, argue about Travis Kelce until six, and by kickoff neither of them will be able to feel their legs from the morning run. Marty thinks Allen makes one more throw at the end. Della thinks Mahomes gets the ball with time left, which is the scariest thing in football.

Neither one will be shocked if it comes down to the final snap. That's what these two teams do to each other.

My call: Bills 25, Chiefs 23.

The Broncos vs Steelers prediction for Black Friday comes down to a road team on a five-game winning streak against a home team that hasn't lost at Acrisure Stadium. Steelers +3 gets my spread pick, Over 37.5 gets the over/under nod, and the final reads Broncos 23, Steelers 21.

Pittsburgh lit its 113th city Christmas tree on Light Up Night last Saturday, the event's 65th year, and Dom Petrakis wants one more reason to celebrate before the decorations come down. His Steelers are 4-0 at home and 6-4 overall.

The Formula: Net ratings Pittsburgh Steelers −8.3, Denver Broncos −2.9 (nflverse play-by-play, Nov 24, 2026).

Denver is the better team, and it's playing like it. The Broncos are 8-2 and have won five straight, including 38-24 over Las Vegas on Sunday. Bo Nix has 12 touchdown throws against five interceptions, and Alex Singleton has 118 tackles behind a defense that has allowed 210 points.

But the Steelers haven't lost at home, and a three-point spread against an unbeaten home team is too much. Pittsburgh's two straight losses came on the road, 38-18 at Cincinnati and 19-16 at Philadelphia. At Acrisure, T.J. Watt has a crowd behind him and 7.5 sacks to his name, Jaylen Warren has 747 rushing yards, and Aaron Rodgers has 16 touchdown throws. Lorna Haskell will tell you Denver doesn't care where the game is played. The road record is 3-2, so the building matters a little.

Both teams have five days of rest, and Denver crosses half the country to get there.

The room tilts to Pittsburgh on the side and goes all the way to the Over. The Formula has Steelers 20, Broncos 24, and lays the 3 with Denver. Next Man Up has Steelers 21, Broncos 22. Letdown Watch has Steelers 21, Broncos 23. In The Trenches has Steelers 20, Broncos 22. Those three take Pittsburgh +3. All four card scores are on Over 37.5. Follow The Money has no pick on either.

The Over is about how low the number sits. The forecast is low 40s with gusts in the 20s, and that's already baked into 37.5. Pittsburgh has scored 214 and allowed 201, and Denver has scored 236 and allowed 210, so both teams' games have run well past 38 points this year. Broncos 23, Steelers 21 adds up to 44, six and a half points clear of 37.5, and a two-point Denver win keeps Pittsburgh inside the 3.

Dom gets a close game and a reason to walk back downtown to the tree either way. Lorna gets the win, and she still has to buy the hot chocolate.

games.fanatic_story:
Downtown Pittsburgh is still glowing from last Saturday. Light Up Night turned 65 this year, with Zambelli fireworks above the rivers, bridges lit up and the city's 113th Christmas tree switched on in front of the City-County Building. Dom Petrakis was on Grant Street for all of it, holding his granddaughter on his shoulders and a Terrible Towel in his back pocket, because you never know.

Lorna Haskell landed from Denver on Wednesday and wanted to know why everyone in the airport was already talking about Friday.

Dom: Because it's Black Friday, it's three o'clock, and it's the Steelers at home. Nobody's shopping. The malls are going to be empty and the stadium is going to be shaking.

Lorna: Your team lost its last two.

Dom: We don't lose at home. Four games at Acrisure, four wins. Ask Atlanta. Ask Cincinnati. Ask Indianapolis. Ask Cleveland.

That's the whole Pittsburgh argument, and it's a good one. The Steelers have been a different team in their own building. The trouble is the road. A blowout in Cincinnati and a gut punch in Philadelphia have Dom's neighbors in Carrick calling the radio shows again, and that's never a good sign in this town.

Lorna's Broncos come in on a heater. Denver has won five in a row and beat Las Vegas going away last Sunday. The Broncos lost the opener in Kansas City and a game in San Francisco early on, and since then they've been the team nobody wants to see on the schedule.

Lorna: Alex Singleton has a hundred and eighteen tackles. A hundred and eighteen. He's in on every play like he's paying rent there.

Dom: T.J. Watt doesn't need a hundred tackles. He needs one good one on your quarterback.

Watt has seven and a half sacks, and Dom has a rule: if Watt gets home on the first series, the whole stadium comes alive. Lorna's answer is Bo Nix, who has twelve touchdown throws and only five interceptions and doesn't panic when the pocket caves. Jaylen Waddle gives him somebody fast to look for, and J.K. Dobbins keeps the chains moving when the wind kicks up.

The wind is going to howl. The forecast for Friday afternoon says low forties with gusts past twenty, and Dom has never been happier about a weather report.

Dom: That's Pittsburgh football. Nobody's throwing the ball sixty yards in that. You hand it to Jaylen Warren and you make them tackle him. Seven hundred and forty-seven yards. He runs angry.

Lorna: Our defense eats running backs.

Dom: Your defense never ate in Pittsburgh in November.

Aaron Rodgers is the part that makes this weird for both of them. Dom still can't get used to the old man in black and gold, and every time Rodgers finds DK Metcalf on a back-shoulder throw, Dom yells like he's been a fan for twenty years. Lorna thinks Rodgers has two great quarters left in him per game, tops. Dom thinks that's all he needs.

Both teams had five days to get ready after their Sunday games, and both coaching staffs will know exactly what's coming. This is the kind of game that turns on one turnover, one long punt, one third down where somebody gets a hand on the ball.

Dom has a plan for after the game, win or lose. He's walking his granddaughter back downtown to see the tree again, because a lit tree on a cold night fixes most things. Lorna has decided to come along. She says she wants to see if the city still looks that pretty after a home loss.

Dom: You'll find out the other way, kid.

Lorna: We'll see who's buying the hot chocolate.

My call: Broncos 23, Steelers 21.
